about.title: Blythe Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Blythe sits along a stretch of Interstate 10 that carries heavy commercial and commuter traffic through Riverside County, and public crash records show that in the most recent reporting year, 22 injury collisions occurred in the city, with one resulting in a traffic death. For families left behind after a fatal crash on I-10, W Hobson Way, or another local corridor, California law provides a path to pursue a wrongful death claim, though it comes with strict limits on who may file and a firm two-year deadline from the date of death. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that helps connect grieving families in Blythe with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened, explain your options, and pursue compensation for funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of a loved one's companionship. There's never a fee unless the attorney recovers for your family.

whyChoose.title: Why Blythe Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand Who Can File
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases to a spouse, domestic partner, and children first, with certain dependents or heirs eligible in other circumstances. An attorney in our network can help clarify where your family stands before the two-year deadline passes.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. These civil claims are separate from any criminal case tied to the crash.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to Your Family
items.desc: Attorneys connected through LawProactive work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation for your family. You can focus on grieving while someone else handles the legal groundwork.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Blythe?
items.answer: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a public road authority, may share responsibility for a crash on a roadway like I-10, the deadline can be much shorter, so it helps to act quickly.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim under California law?
items.answer: A surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children generally have the first right to file. If none of those survivors exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible, and an independent attorney can help determine exactly who qualifies in your family's situation.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect us with an attorney?
items.answer: No, our service is completely free to grieving families in Blythe and throughout Riverside County. If an independent attorney takes your case, they work on contingency, meaning payment only comes from a recovery, not out of your pocket.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to any criminal charges against the other driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal prosecution that may follow a fatal crash. Your family can pursue compensation through the civil courts regardless of whether criminal charges are filed or how that case turns out.
